name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 205 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 37% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 205 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 37 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Prime Minister Modi is traveling to Bastar in Chhattisgarh to celebrate Diwali with security forces, marking a public display of gratitude in an area once dominated by Naxalites. In Kashmir, a blast at a police outpost in Ghaziabad was claimed by a Kashmir-linked outfit, prompting an ATS investigation while only one local terrorist remains active. Manipur security forces are conducting search operations and holding fortnightly security reviews after a gunfight in Kangpokpi and a rally in Ukhrul demanding an end to ethnic violence. Naxalites in the Bastar Maoist belt have dumped 900 detonators and electronic equipment. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Statsminister Modi reiser til Bastar i Chhattisgarh for å feire Diwali sammen med sikkerhetsstyrker, og markerer en offentlig takknemlighet i et område som tidligere var dominert av naxalitter. I Kashmir ble en bombe detonert ved en politistasjon i Ghaziabad, og en Kashmir-tilknyttet gruppe tok ansvar, noe som har ført til en etterforskning av ATS mens kun én lokal terrorist fortsatt er aktiv. Sikkerhetsstyrker i Manipur gjennomfører søkeoperasjoner og holder to-ukentlige sikkerhetsvurderinger etter en skuddveksling i Kangpokpi og en demonstrasjon i Ukhrul som krevde en slutt på etnisk vold. Naxalitter i den maoistiske beltet i Bastar har dumpet 900 detonatorer og elektronisk utstyr. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
